title: Central banks sit still while oil, AI and an election do the moving
dek: The Fed, ECB and Bank of Japan all held rates; Lagarde announced an early exit; Hormuz attacks swung crude; and an AI spending scare knocked the Nasdaq.

mood.label: Nervous
mood.explanation: The VIX — the options market's gauge of expected S&P 500 swings — sat at 19.41 on 2 November, up about a quarter over the month, and CNN's Fear & Greed index was at 25, "extreme fear", down from 30 a week earlier. High-yield credit spreads widened to 3.26 percentage points on 29 October from 3.14 the day before, and Reddit chatter skewed towards index trackers and leveraged chip bets rather than calm.

regions.headline: Fed on hold, tech wobbles, voters go to the polls
regions.summary: The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged on 28 October, saying it wanted more information even though inflation is still elevated. An AI-spending scare pushed the Nasdaq Composite down 2% on the week and 6.45% over the month to 30 October. Midterm elections on 3 November and the October jobs report give markets two more things to digest.

regions.headline: Growth of 0.4% and a surprise exit at the ECB
regions.summary: Euro area GDP rose 0.4% in the third quarter, with Germany beating expectations and France contracting. The ECB held rates at a 2.5% deposit rate, and Christine Lagarde said she will step down early, in February. The Bank of England is expected to raise rates this week, which matters for UK households remortgaging.

regions.headline: BoJ holds, China factories shrink, Korea rebounds
regions.summary: The Bank of Japan kept rates steady while saying underlying inflation has reached its 2% target; the yen was near 157.89 per dollar. China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October, below the 50 line that separates growth from contraction. The KOSPI jumped 7.12% on the week on chip and AI news, though it is still down 15.59% over the month.

Reserve Bank of Australia meeting and Australian housing data
body:
## The week in one paragraph

Three big central banks met and all three did nothing. The Federal Reserve [held rates steady](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikAFBVV95cUxPaU93czlpTHJXMTJGby0yOGppZGVlVkZzZW4tNC11WTcwVk1yQUZHTVMza0dTLURMRi0tTUtYTHhITkI2OVBWN2k0anZCN2liNnlyNFpaTmFTaWlFTHItWmtBXzh1VWhkRjZBNjVDejQxOGNUTW1HWWRBUzNjbGdKUDV0MlFSWXRsaWQwMXpWQXI?oc=5) on 28 October, [so did the European Central Bank](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxOcG81Z2FUM3Y0clJEaWJ6SFhSRU5Ed3JuVUZGZXZpOXRBZVN4YmhWMUJ2eDZJNWttc1NCV0dxWFVWV0ppM2d5OE1zVDZ5V1RyMHFUbGdQcG9QelFheHQwMl9oRUwwX3V0SEpCdGxJcVVvbVFDTU5CeVdzSXA3WEhuT1pWa1JsWXdNTksxd2pPQjBmSmd0c3g3YjZlV1dxamF3eEQxOWp4YTVpRWE3UmRoT3lXZ2hfNzVOTFFCZzVPZw?oc=5), and [the Bank of Japan kept policy unchanged](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxNSnRoUnFPTXd3aThEbHFYOXpiS2RwcUhURmhyc2RVMWtxdENYOGg0cjVYWllUS012TnI2Rmxxd3d2dEx4QURuVW9ZWUhFdzVuOHNvWlpYOV9Rd0xCNHRfNTNuMVFZeVQwOUZ1ZHVlTkFnMUllanAwRkQzLXMyaE9qMzY1Vmp4Vy1GU0NTYVpLbkQ5eG5PVXlSYUh0T0l2YjJ3RVVIX0hzUmM?oc=5) while saying inflation has finally reached its target. The real movement came from elsewhere: attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil up and then back down again as peace talk emerged, a spending scare hit the biggest artificial-intelligence companies, and Christine Lagarde announced she is leaving the ECB early. American voters go to the polls on Tuesday. Markets ended the week jittery rather than panicked: the S&P 500 closed at 7,580.07 on 30 October, down 0.57% on the week, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 2%.

## United States

The Fed left its policy rate alone, saying it wanted an "accumulation of more information" before moving again, [despite inflation it called elevated](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxQTE1BdGtmWVdsaDdsWktpYlk1d2lzWGN2OGdvc3VSNFZxcC1EZ0lWVHhuT1ZpOWphTHoxMzlVY2U2cWxKZDNIZVBhTkR4OXNzbW5fVG41SFZ1b0U1cHFtempLQzVQQmRuQmhpWVJXdy1mV2NxSERSZjZqVnJRZkRJR1diMFY1dkxT?oc=5). It is easy to see why it is stuck. September CPI inflation was 4.02% year on year, up from 3.71% in August, but core inflation — which strips out food and energy — was much calmer at 2.79%. In other words, the headline jump is largely an energy story, and energy is being set in the Gulf rather than in Washington. Unemployment was 4.2% in September, a touch above August's 4.1%.

Borrowing costs stayed high. The 10-year Treasury yield, the benchmark for corporate borrowing and US mortgages, closed at 4.93% on 30 October; the two-year was 4.61% on 29 October. The gap between the two — the "yield curve", which shows whether investors demand more to lend for longer — was a positive 0.38 percentage points, the normal shape, but at a high level overall. For finance directors that means refinancing in 2027 will not be obviously cheaper than refinancing today.

Equities had an uncomfortable month. The Nasdaq is down 6.45% over four weeks, while the Russell 2000 index of smaller companies actually rose 1.29% on the week — a rotation away from the biggest technology names rather than a broad retreat. This week brings the October jobs report and [the midterm elections on 3 November](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxONHhuUTlfWTZEWmR2REVvZnJQcEJFX2dpLWFqV0t1WnJUVjZIN1BXUGJNMW5zbGVxQXhUaXY3MWlya1lCNlhkYTFEY2Y3bGxTVVBoOXRERmh0WlAtcWZvTWtQcWNlV1VKVFo2SGt4aXhtTjN2SlZhWnVJT0VmRmpjSzZITGZaSTNtUlNzc1lUaThNRlVSckhRREo3UHdVUkpGcnc?oc=5), with investors already [gaming out what different outcomes in Congress mean for spending and AI policy](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxPSndxQlZKTnRLd3BYVTNReUZRU1Z5dDlrdGpidzBlWVhITzgzTkJrXzJlNlhHZHZvQS1JV0E3YUZmT3gzNy1KbWVGVGs4NjR0bVFDanJ4RjYybjU2Rm9DS2tNR0w3SVNpb0puX2NwUjctM1U2cm1EYmZRUWRXd08tY1dfT1BGYmF0TG5UREVHTUVfM0s5MGhHZE1EVVhVUlRCbk5tZmExZU8zUi05bm9B?oc=5).

## Euro area

The economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter, [with France contracting while the bloc as a whole held up](https://news.google.?oc=5). [German inflation cooled, helped by a fuel tax cut, and the German economy grew more than expected](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOT2VyTFJQdHM3YjBFYUJJbDA4Y0JfSFZUTm5XNDloeUJCeUlRcU4wdEtvNXJISGtKc0h3MHFCajg5YTEtYUh6NkJ0eWxmdTRJOEtfRnh5OUFBUUpGNWdQV1FUY2NRN2tMbllZVUFDZWhqVG9SUjR3X2xnOXdDQkJiQUdxWGVkWEN6ZVNsdUprZnBmWlpOT0JSa0w4LTlzSHdfX3U0?oc=5). Euro area HICP inflation was 3.75% in September, up from 3.23% in August, and unemployment held at 6.5% — low by the region's own history.

The week's surprise was personnel, not policy. [Lagarde said she will step down in February, nine months early](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxNemp5dVBmbU1jdWFEX1pWbmZzSUxhbDU4bzBXdEM4cWw4UTBYMDBERnZId051WTVyekp4NDZLQUlXLU40NE95LXhnUTE4S1hISlZKV3prVkNTOS1rREZ1dVloeVlkSGtVdmNmbWhRck9hTTkwbWZhT3ZaVjliWkRwQ01JeXA?oc=5), telling reporters [she could not remain neutral on world events](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOZldaRFJxZExRTzZ2T1lfc1pYUWtpbFJwRHk0YmpCaHdkYXd4ZV9vbGpmellrN1Ztck8wallTMnphd1V6VWFLckM4bTRiX1c5VmZmSUZwdUROem02ZXlUY3NKT1poTEhFWDRQOThHcEQ5YkMzY1gxU1NoTm5mdFhVR2xWakJSYUFVSTRKS0Rva1JIR0FhOHFJck5Ic3AzNzNWQTJuMXFySnNFcDNIYXN0TWtn?oc=5) and, as several outlets framed it, [allowing EU leaders to choose a successor before France's elections](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxQT0ZULXZqVG03S2wtMFE5SHVoS1c4SmZmSUhxTzRjSFdTdllkOFliM1Ewa1MxTjhaTS0yYUQ3QW9xODRrR0xjNHlBZkItQlBrc2NMdGgwR3EzVlN4UXpJeFZlOEdqX3ZhWjJaZ0w0SEVhTnBOTUZodmh1ampsYmI5dC1kTlB5ZXVFcWJURg?oc=5). The deposit rate stayed at 2.5%. French government bond yields were already the highest of the big three at 4.48% in September, against 3.47% in Germany, a reminder that politics still shows up in national borrowing costs.

In Britain, [the Bank of England is expected to raise rates this week, while possibly pushing back on bets for more](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxPOFVxcW9DcnR5S1BVdndGZkhXT1F1SUR0WEZTbkRsSzRLSmtiOXFZdXNneUs4VXVCaV9ldFZQVVdHMnVvWDBrZERDTFo5bHc4NE9GelZKbmloVi1VVTVmN0tiZXFUSW5fMFIzMXZCWE5CWHd5TEdHc2VvRVA3T1VCRV9XampjTDBmd3BpTlkyNjBScTJReVhCanlUX21XX1dhbWc?oc=5). [Millions of households are due to remortgage onto worse deals](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxPR0xfdi1WS1FBanVxeHdBd1MyaGdDaE9WSDdHUTVBNlRwZmxfd3lYOVVkVkMzTVB1b0g5VWo1SEtaVDZGRzdjMTFOY044dTBycDlMLUp3dHFUcmlkRG5oeEV0eGl4cGQ4bjdRdXBPWlBXYjAxQ3YzdUhDdUlVOTIzVHhDY1VNbnc3TWZMWVc1LUQwQQ?oc=5) — a direct hit to disposable income. Away from markets, [Gen Z protests in Germany turned violent](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQYmIyNllhTkFrTXZlQ3ZqZkhUczVpY0ZqZzlONFdfUXdpWU95VkxfMy1oazdjclhEYlJSRVRac0MtcTAyak5GNGNsNXBER0Y2Vk1uRm95aDBZX292LVJDb0dlVzJLR1k0VW04Q01Cb0FaR05ZUG81WnFHZ2tWbW16YjBraU5pcVZKV0IzNGxIZzZ4MmVzRG5KeXN1YzlmN2MwdURPVXJMUDRlT1NfSExn?oc=5) as [unrest in France eased](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxPX0QtNjJvRnpjT3Y5eTVBcEI5dkZMaFNuZnJDMkR1cWY5aWRWV2FjX3QxVVVHNUZRMlp1VFBYYnpCdE1NcmRqQlUtbVV0akY5RUF5WXdjaXcxYnBtNk4xZDhJNmtKWGlaTGhkcTltaW9TTHlBTmdlU0I1cFlVbjdmckVaMDBaTllsNmJCYWlZM0NCaFZsdk00b3Z4bV9BYlhiSnhZ?oc=5), and [Bulgaria elected a new president](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## Asia

The Bank of Japan held, but with a notable line: [it judged that trend inflation has hit the 2% target](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxNcnhYX2pTREQwTVpVRkliZlptQl81YWowMUtRS1VSYU5nN1BsR3ZvWjlxMTkyVXk3Y2VuMktGR2k2M3AxTTQ2dmo2aVRBRlNreHBxb1pFeWtIb2VzbW56UHpsRDEteGVJTXluYmthbWVWWVNWaWpMcmduTDRMMXRTdjZuSkpHX084a2tEblN5NDVLVzMzTmVuRE9SWWV1TUptN1JWOUYyMFU3OEp0WEt6YkhkTHN2Zw?oc=5). [Tokyo CPI rose 2.8% in October](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxNNzdEOWZBcTJGM0pORlRMVW1SUVpiSWdFYkZJMW5yYlZxTk5GUk5Zblp3Y2lCTERBTjBoSDhicW02YzZaOXRYRmhlc1hhUDNWSnA4MG01bzdtTExhMDZJdl83bW9SbXp6Z1kxdlp5SXJzTmVnd0ZDZ0pOTllJU08tZHJDZXBpTUhJVXdjYTFBcDFHbmU0YjJscHRkOTUzc2Mx?oc=5), and [core inflation stayed above target ahead of the decision](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxPUVJOQjlQV2RMWlM5UDhDcTIxN1RCOFVwYWxOOElaZGxWRTRJajZ2YzNLM2wzeGlBNW9KYkxiVW1LZUNrbjlpNUdFeGJQQmYxdnhDZXR0TTRSWkpGUGdxdFA4RUtOdWJMUmdQR0lmd1RIQVAxa2FaMURNaVVkZEZzTkg3X0pnY1d0MEhLOVhDVkxzS2p1VWpkbjkxTjcxSG1VYW90cg?oc=5). The yen was at 157.89 to the dollar, barely changed on the week; Japan's 10-year yield was 3.05% in September, a level that would have been unthinkable a few years ago. The Nikkei rose 1.43% on the week but is down 9.81% over the month.

China went the other way. [The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October, with the non-manufacturing index at 49.7](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxQVGF6cGFuMDFPSlQ4T1dBc0ZWcEVBOEtmVmFKaW5PSWkzOXJhQ3JzaXVDb1RhYTZ1Yk1rdDhJa0oycmFOdEZjU3FEeldpYnUzM1FDQUVYLUlJVzNyVWdKd082WmtBSWtQaFFpWmh5SFdRLXRVWTdpaHRSTUlHY3czV1RNRkVUUUcyakh5S1ZkZ0NTSHB6OFFWRGR3RFZNOUZMejJsdHdJWExtbDJkdExfa0d6QUliTkszOG1xTg?oc=5) — both below the 50 mark, meaning activity is shrinking. [New export orders weakened](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxOUjYxcFNzbUhDZ2VfVXowN2ZEM0ppaVNFV2NMT0h1aHBZZGZSRkVRMGQwNGpGc0ZBb2hYbXdjSWVoc0VoNE1xWENGLTdOcWswcWdVaW55TmlybjFNVnUzMGMyQ1lLVTM0Q0FWNDdILWx4cUszekVUMGRSenVnNXdfZXpOTmVnSW16bWVzTGFqRHFoMDNtUWFfUUxsYlQ5U3ZZ?oc=5), and [it was the third contraction in four months](https://news.google.?oc=5). The Shanghai Composite fell 1.61% on the week. India looks very different: [the RBI raised its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2% while projecting 7.1% GDP growth](https://news.google.?oc=5), and [the finance ministry pegged second-quarter growth at 7.35%](https://news.google.?oc=5). The Sensex gained 2.83%. Korea's KOSPI jumped 7.12% as [investors looked past the US tech rout](https://news.google.?oc=5). Elsewhere, [Australia's housing slump deepened as the RBA prepares another rate rise](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuwFBVV95cUxONzMzYXY1WFZINk5mclI1MmtHUlBMVElDN1I1NXljaFgyXzRPenE1ZnBhZUhsNEp2bE0xdmczT2F0NHBfWDVHTTNJVVpfU2xIc2tQLTU2X3ROZ2g4WmJwaXQ4dXduX1B3RmtEWjVtSVV2S3c5cjNYY245LXNXYW5HbFk5UGhWYkpXTHVLZzM2ZE1DRzhxa2xUdUcyWUdGeXhfeTZzT0lfQi1admtJN2Z2cElxQjBXZnp6WlRn?oc=5), and [Taiwan accused China of harassment after a standoff between ships](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxPLWl6Yi00bDFaUUJsWkpTdHlRT0h3eE9aUTJrcW9DT1ZvQ2YtQjZ2MlliR1l2WGZ6VHdIUE41X1Y0Z0Q5UUNqRVpKTnZMc3VvdjduNWRLY3RjRHZRUkhwcnB3Ny1QN3NFMURxNlVTZ3J6Zl9JN3piUC1CeFdMcE05WmFrbw?oc=5).

## Debt and politics

Oil dominated. [Iran's IRGC Navy said two tankers exploded after hitting mines in Hormuz](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxNZmk2dmxjdk1sOW96UkZiaUlJVXhzc1pJMjZJUnY2WGtvaXd4aXRJY3d4UTNoUmFJdUVQQjlkb0JPSmxEc2YzS1JOZ2NSWmpTUnhzYzBiU1hfeXBvb2F2WEp2NHc5YkFfUUNKSHc2NW1PMUVKT0xqUTdOa0tfUmZpQWE2SDFtdzJ5TmZleWpLd0Zid1JWR2Z0d0dOeVMwekFzNTNTYndHMmMyV0poZ2h0UmFOVWc2M3o3Z2h6TUR2SQ?oc=5), [with ships carrying around 2m barrels affected](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxQajJOOUdQdDNTMl9uOTZQN1RqUTdxQnJXUjVYZU4tUkRfenZ4MXBIemFHR2x6cVNHemU2R2dybG90TkZtbFRuTDQ1N3liZ0t1NHhUZlA1R2t2UEl0OUZnLV9NODBEbEhKX1BqNi01c2pWWnp2cXRxNEpRSWpPT195N3FXUzA4NVZObl9JRERnb3B0eTdmOUxV?oc=5), though [tankers kept crude flowing](https://news.google.?oc=5). Then on Monday [prices fell more than 4% as peace talks eased supply fears](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxNSGlnQ2hWb0xhREU3dG5ZeGtaV3cxb1kzRk9TT2FOanNnRW8yWWVkd0xCLWpmbDRLVkVqRVpMWXJuY2E1N2tfMGRnV3hkWE1IRmtjYWU0M3Z0V1FlMmoyaTlGSXl2Y1R1ZVZYUUdvdnJnZjNVRzBTNzhtb0FnaWJuV3hhWkpVQU1iRkVtSmFhWjQ0XzM3T0NBVmFudVVldWhZemFoeDJPSy1hWXhCbmdEbUVB?oc=5), leaving Brent at 108.63 a barrel, down 6.2% on the week but still 8.28% higher over the month. That swing is the single biggest input into household fuel bills and freight costs right now. Meanwhile [nine big oil firms are on track to share more than $95bn of profit for a second straight quarter](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxQeXBJYWlwMjdwM3djOG81dHVZNHlIX1dUZWM2dEYya2YzOVp1TTR6bmN1dm9hbWxqLU5zMFYzYTVtTzFkOHdVdG9hWGlaWmEtaGM2dmlveGVCODZDY3FiYk5BeTFaLW5QeF9FVGxPQmdBOWwteEc5bjFZMTh2d0I2c2NCVm94VTlHT1M1REhIWU9WeTJReTFRV3ZfWm5rc05EUWFjLTN2dHhETE1pWXRNWS0xOFZ0dw?oc=5).

On debt, [Wall Street is bracing for the biggest overhaul of Treasury issuance in years](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxQQ3N2ZVdrWVZaekU3UUdvbWgzZE4wTUF5X2tsajg4V042UDRJeEpwa2RqY1RxLWlNNk5sWTl4QUFlQk1mQjhsTzh3STlDR0lVN3ByaVQyUFRFUnlpZG95dGpuZjVtN3lMX3lfQkZRWnUyM3FqSnAyeE9sQ25fSHI1Mmo2M1dPT3d4RkwxM1hjSkRYbFBrdlFtUXpnUlNCc05aRkJvOWNFSFZBQjRqaXFHUVVGZzQ?oc=5), with [long-bond cuts and greater reliance on short-dated bills in focus](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTFB2dTI4WFBnRWpmUlBmYUxmUTZJeEYzUFIyVzdwWEU5bGt0UEVEdTBrcXpnX3lwTG5NcnJtWkYxOHpINVM5Wkx0OGZHZVNObEdncUhxRmZUUW1rSkM0V3Y4VlVsN1B2Wjl4aC12bDY4NzdnU1NVYmc?oc=5). US federal debt was 121.19% of GDP in the second quarter, and [commentators argue the Treasury is now managing debt costs as much as inflation](https://news.google.?oc=5). Euro area government debt was 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter.

## AI and technology

The AI trade had its worst stretch in a while. [Big Tech shed close to $900bn in a rout over soaring AI spending](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxOSnZtb2F5QWc3U085dm1WalA2WEV0VnhyYnN4azV0WE9yRDhtSGRiUXFfTUF4dUkxNTYyMGItYUJxN2k5ZFdXS3hPb09sLVdsc3ZNV2ZqdGwxdm9VN3l6YW42bFVIcjdSS2ZjdFJyYlNCQVBiazU4dGhBVDRGYW9wLUhiZEU?oc=5), and [the Nasdaq faced a roughly $2trn wipeout in October as those fears deepened](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxPNkNDLXpLZ1A0VklROTJVenpDRlZBWE10ZE1qWWk4ZFVqalgzWWJFdThSd2ZKeUhDanVRQjRhVVVZZGlGZzY1UWYzLXRSZTNHNDNPTkZZRUFJazAzYmV6NzF3QUJtNjhkWHY5OHZNZWVsSFdyY0NScGJadnE3T0dPTWtBUXZOaDJPYWJuX1NOVXkwbGlQSW9MdjlXTlNQTzdLZEdzTHFsQ2gzaEcwTkNHZTNCNF9hMG9lazFHRXItSzg?oc=5); [Google and Microsoft held off raising their capital-spending forecasts](https://news.google.?oc=5). Against that, [Anthropic plans to sell up to $3.5bn of shares to Japanese investors as part of its US IPO](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixAFBVV95cUxOazUtcTBWVFNLd21jTk9YOFRDRHoyc2ZuV1haZ21JaUdIei1leFkxVVF5V0JpLXJGdV9raXhrV0k0bU1xM0g5TnR6cTA5dWNFZ3VVVUo1UHVyU3pUUWw0YjFreXNTZ3Q4TXdoazBwT1dxRU52bTkxMXlEbG95LVY1eUlLMGZHUk9hQUd4aVZxWkxMUzBMVmhELWNpaUhSaGR3V19UYy00R3UzMUVkWU80ZHl0aW9URGdlQ19RX2dmZHFreHNS?oc=5), and [Marvell agreed to buy optical-components maker Lumentum in a $115bn deal aimed at AI data centres](https://news.google.?oc=5). The gap between enthusiasm for AI infrastructure deals and nervousness about who pays for it is the defining market tension of the moment.

## Company news and results

Reported figures this week were mixed across sectors. Linde, the industrial gases group, [reported third-quarter sales of $9,404m, up 9% year on year, with diluted EPS of $3.66, down 11%, and adjusted EPS of $4.59, up 9%](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1707925/000165495426009199/lin_ex991.htm), in its SEC filing; it guided full-year adjusted EPS to $17.82–$17.92 and capital expenditure of $5.5bn–$6.0bn. Volumes grew fastest in electronics, chemicals and energy — the same end markets feeding the data-centre build-out.

In deals and incidents: [Marvell's purchase of Lumentum was confirmed](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOelFpUlRuWUdrd3oyYkZTNkxFMW9mQlBTY01YTl9ERVRsYTc1VGNWQjR1VF90aEcwY01sTDNXN3NiWVBZNTY4aGVFSlR3WlBlb0laSkptRS1EMF9fMGlna1BXSVExN2dFVGlTNWMyQzYyM1RsYm5pMGxXOWxhbmp1UGRYVjk3RVA0b25WWVZPcFZMS05IOE1CTUgzY1BsQWY3MW5DbDF1bGs1M185UlM4cjlB?oc=5) after [earlier reports of advanced talks](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxNR2xWTFdaYmFQNV9rVnZVcmltcTJqWGoyUVBzUlVPcDJaZm4xLXVCMmt4Szk2YnF1VjVXUEdjV0xDbGxRdjc2WjBzQjVnTnU0SWpSWkJmdlg0WS15eGNhc09ZNWpHUVc2Znk0aE9haUpPVlZOeUdqNl9CSzdHaUtITm1BTWh1d0tKTWtCYWM1M183ekZkSGptb3B4MUthVzhiM1hUOEhR?oc=5); [the FBI linked North Korea's TraderTraitor group to a record $6.43bn crypto heist at Binance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxQWmVOUTJ5cEo0bUU2Unp2V093dXNIN3hEaHB5VXRrZlBYRjc5RkVzM2lraGRpZGNIM0s0Uk15bVdPOHNSNGJsN29Ma3lVTzBleWd2WHRuSGlzOXVtV193RE8wbXgyaGNjdGdJRkUxdkR2ajN0MGh2STQ2T2p3YTVMTnRVME8?oc=5); and [supermarket freezers in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg were hit by a suspected cyber-attack](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTFBhcE44b2ZsOG9fMFFnNTY4Q3hZUDk5QW9Oa1JkUkRKLVJhcGJHellrUU5kdExKNVpGRnJhbHJSZjRhODJfa0xhN05iQ2czckM3TjJ4TU5WQ1Z0T00?oc=5) — a reminder that operational resilience is now a board-level cost line.

## Market mood

Fear is the word. The VIX stood at 19.41 on 2 November, up about 25% over the month, and CNN's Fear & Greed index fell to 25 — "extreme fear" — from 30 a week earlier and 38 a month ago. High-yield credit spreads, the extra interest riskier companies pay over the government, widened to 3.26 percentage points on 29 October from 3.14 the previous day: a nudge wider, not a credit event. Gold fell 3.19% on the week to 3,909.40 and bitcoin dropped 4.49%, so this was not a simple flight to safety. On Reddit, attention was split between broad index trackers and a cluster of chip and AI names — unverified opinion, but it suggests retail investors are still watching the same story as everyone else.
